Run an MCP server for R tools over stdio

Source: R/mcp_server.R
mcp_server.Rd

mcp_server() runs a Model Context Protocol server over standard input and output. It exposes tools created with mcplite::tool() so MCP clients can discover and call R functions. Compatible ellmer::tool() objects can also be supplied when users already use ellmer, but ellmer is not required for ordinary mcplite tools.

Usage

mcp_server(tools, instructions = NULL)

Arguments

tools

Tool definitions to expose. Supply one mcplite::tool() object or a list of tool definitions. Compatible ellmer::tool() objects are accepted when supplied directly.

instructions

Optional server instructions to advertise to clients using a protocol version that supports them.

Value

mcp_server() is called for its side effect of serving MCP requests. It blocks the current R process until standard input closes.

Run a server

Supply one tool or a list of tools directly. Put the complete setup in a script that defines or sources tools and ends with mcplite::mcp_server(actual_tool_or_list). Configure the MCP client to launch it with Rscript --vanilla /absolute/path/to/server.R; use an absolute script path because the client's working directory is not guaranteed. The call blocks until standard input closes, so use a client-launched script rather than an interactive R console.

Tools may return ordinary R values for text conversion or opt into native content and structured output with tool_result(). See mcplite-results for exact mappings and payload JSON options. Set those options before constructing results and starting the server, and keep them stable while it runs. Tools own input validation, output conformance, permissions, and safe side effects; schemas are not authorization or sandboxing.

Keep stdout exclusively for MCP protocol messages. Send diagnostics and telemetry to stderr or a remote exporter, not stdout.

Server scope

mcplite is a tools-only, stdio-only server. It does not implement JSON-RPC batching, HTTP transports, sessions, prompts, resource listing or reading, subscriptions, cancellation, sampling, elicitation, roots, Tasks, MCP Apps, progress notifications, or server-initiated and other multi-round-trip requests. Embedded resource blocks are self-contained, and resource links do not make their URIs readable through mcplite.

Protocol compatibility

The same server definition supports four MCP versions. A tool remains available when its output schema cannot be represented by the client's protocol. Compatible explicit or generated text content remains available when structured content is omitted. Tool authors still own full schema validity and runtime input/output conformance.

MCP versionLifecycleOutput schemasStructured contentAudio, resource links, per-content metadata
2026-07-28Protocol selected per requestEvery supported shapeEvery supported JSON valueSupported
2025-11-25initialize firstDirect object-root onlyObject values onlySupported
2025-06-18initialize firstDirect object-root onlyObject values onlySupported
2024-11-05initialize firstOmittedOmittedUnsupported

Text, images, embedded resources, annotations, and result metadata work in every supported version. A 2024-11-05 call returning audio or a resource link receives a contained tool-level error instead of partial content or server termination.

Modern 2026-07-28 clients select the protocol with per-request metadata. server/discover, tools/list, and tools/call do not require initialize. Discovery advertises 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, and 2024-11-05 in that preference order. Every successful modern result includes resultType = "complete" and the server's canonical identity in _meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]. Modern server/discover and tools/list results also include public cache hints with a 300000 millisecond TTL. Modern ping is unsupported. Legacy clients retain ping, tools/list, and tools/call after initialization.

OpenTelemetry tracing

mcplite automatically creates one OpenTelemetry server span for every parsed MCP request or notification that passes JSON-RPC envelope validation. This includes retained legacy initialization and ping, notifications, modern discovery, tool listing and calls, and valid unknown methods. Blank input, JSON parse failures, and malformed JSON-RPC envelopes do not create MCP operation spans.

Tool authors do not need to call otel::start_local_active_span() for the MCP operation or tool invocation. The server span remains active while tool code runs, so optional tool-authored spans can become children without being required. mcplite does not create a redundant automatic tool-execution child span.

Provider and exporter configuration belongs to the standard otel and otelsdk environment variables and APIs. mcplite does not add telemetry arguments, choose an exporter, or configure a provider. With no exporter configured, tracing is an effective no-op and MCP behavior is unchanged. A safe stderr configuration is OTEL_R_TRACES_EXPORTER=stderr Rscript --vanilla /absolute/path/to/server.R; a remote exporter such as OTLP is also suitable.

Do not use a stdout or console exporter with a stdio MCP server. Standard output is reserved exclusively for MCP protocol messages, so telemetry written there will corrupt the protocol stream.

Remote W3C parent context may be supplied in params._meta.traceparent, with optional params._meta.tracestate. Malformed propagation data is ignored, and _meta is not passed to tool functions. By default, spans contain selected low-cardinality operation metadata; raw requests and responses, tool arguments and results, _meta, trace headers, and condition messages are not recorded as span attributes.

Examples

if (identical(Sys.getenv("MCPLITE_CAN_BLOCK_PROCESS"), "true")) {
  add_numbers <- tool(
    function(x, y) {
      x + y
    },
    name = "add_numbers",
    description = "Add two numbers and return the result.",
    arguments = list(
      x = type_number("First number."),
      y = type_number("Second number.")
    )
  )

  mcp_server(list(add_numbers))
}
